title: Epic maps on a common rank-one slice are invertible
statement: Let X be a scheme, O a sheaf of commutative rings on its pro-etale site, W an object of the site, and f:M -> N an epimorphism of module sheaves over the underlying ring sheaf of O. Suppose the restrictions of M and N to the slice over W each have a specified isomorphism to the regular module restricted to W. Then the restriction of f to W is an isomorphism. No hypotheses away from this slice, flatness, finiteness, or nonzero coefficient rings are needed.

proof_origin.note: Extract a complete proved helper into its own module so every delivered file compiles within the per-file limit.

proof.text: Restriction preserves local surjectivity; forgetting module structure reflects epimorphisms. Conjugate the restricted epic map by its two bases to obtain an epic regular-module endomorphism. This is multiplication by its value on 1. Local preimages of 1 make that value locally a unit; cancel it and use sheaf separatedness to prove injectivity. The endomorphism is mono and epi in the abelian category of module sheaves, hence invertible. Undo the two bases.

theorem diagonalLocalRankOne_isIso (X : Scheme.{u})
    (O : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) CommRingCat.{u + 1}) (W : X.ProEt)
    {M N : SheafOfModules.{u + 1} ((sheafCompose (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj O)}
    (f : M ⟶ N) [Epi f]
    (e : M.over W ≅ (SheafOfModules.unit _).over W)
    (d : N.over W ≅ (SheafOfModules.unit _).over W) : IsIso (f.over W)
